correctness.rationale: For a simplicial \(d\)-polytope, the classical Lower Bound Theorem gives the stacked-polytope lower face numbers \(f_j\ge inom d j f_0-j inom{d+1}{j+1}\) for \(1\le j\le d-2\) and \(f_{d-1}\ge(d-1)f_0-(d+1)(d-2)\). Solving these inequalities gives exactly \(f_0\le\Lambda_{d,j}(f_j)\). The lead source endpoint theorems depend monotonically on the number of vertices or facets through a negative power, so substitution of that upper bound preserves the inequality. Polarity converts a simple circumscribed polytope to a simplicial polar with \(f_k(Q)=f_{d-1-k}(Q^\circ)\), giving the circumscribed statement. No finite computation is used to prove an infinite case.

value.rationale: The lead source explicitly highlights the missing face dimensions as the natural open extension of its radial theory. On two central combinatorial subclasses, the theorem closes that entire range nonasymptotically for every analytic dual-volume deviation, with explicit constants and a sharp combinatorial complexity conversion. This is a structural partial resolution of the source problem rather than a routine parameter substitution: the full simplicial Lower Bound Theorem is strictly stronger than the half-vector inequalities used in the source and its predecessors.
